summary: Layer 12 blurs chemistry by degrading the decodability of additive atomic properties (LogP/MR) and specific topological features (5-membered rings), even when non-linear probes are used, though binary structural flags remain robustly preserved.

claims.claim: For continuous atomic property contributions like Crippen LogP (`crippen_logp_contrib`) and Molecular Refractivity (`mr`), the information is significantly degraded at layer 12 compared to early layers (4-8) for both linear and non-linear decoders, indicating entanglement rather than perfect re-encoding.
claims.evidence: Pretrained `mlp_drop`=10.3 for Crippen; MLP error rises from Err=0.015 at Layer 4 to Err=0.157 at Layer 12 (R2 drops from 0.985 to 0.843). Linear probe shows similar degradation (`lin_drop`=4.5, R2 0.93 -> 0.69).
claims.test: Train an MLP head on atom embeddings at Layer 12 vs Layer 4 using label `crippen_logp_contrib`. Prediction: Mean Absolute Error increases by >8x (e.g., from ~0.015 to >0.1) and R² drops below 0.9.

claims.claim: Binary structural features like aromaticity (`aromatic`) remain decodable at layer 12 with low absolute error (<0.03), despite high relative drop metrics caused by near-zero baseline errors in early layers.
claims.evidence: Pretrained `aromatic` Lin Error L12=0.004, MLP Error L12=0.003; Relative drops are 15x/13x because best layer error is ~0.0 (R²~1.0). Absolute performance remains high compared to Random baseline.
claims.test: Filter atoms with SMARTS `[c]` or `tok_element='C' & tok_in_ring=1`. Train probe on Layer 12 embeddings for label `aromatic`. Prediction: AUROC > 0.995, Error < 0.03.
claims.prediction: Absolute error at L12 remains < 0.03 despite high drop ratio.

claims.claim: The degradation pattern is specific to learned representations; random-initialized models show no depth-related performance loss (Drop ~1.0), confirming the 'blur' is a consequence of training dynamics, not architectural layer count.
claims.evidence: Random `mlp_drop`=1.0 for all concepts (e.g., Crippen Drop=1.0). Pretrained/a1_step1 drops range 5x-800x depending on baseline error magnitude.
claims.test: Run FixedProbe/MLPProbe on model kind `random` across layers [4,6,8,10,12]. Prediction: Error ratio (L12/Lbest) ≈ 1.0 for all concepts.
claims.prediction: lin_drop and mlp_drop values will be approximately 1.0 ± 0.1.

claims.claim: Non-linear decoding recovers more signal than linear probing at layer 12, but still suffers significant degradation relative to its own best-layer performance (e.g., Layer 4), suggesting information is re-encoded non-linearly rather than discarded entirely.
claims.evidence: Pretrained `crippen` MLP R²=0.843 vs Linear R²=0.689 at L12, yet both drop from Best Layer values (`mlp_drop`=10.3). This indicates the signal exists but is less accessible than in shallow layers.
claims.test: Compare MLP probe performance against FixedProbe on `mr` label at Layer 12 using same seed/mask. Prediction: MLP R² > Linear R² (e.g., 0.87 vs 0.68), but both < Best Layer values.
claims.prediction: MLP error will be lower than Linear error, yet still higher than the probe's own best-layer performance.

claims.claim: The blurring effect is consistent across Pretrained and RTD-only (`a1_step1`) models for regression tasks (e.g., `mr`), implying pretraining objectives drive deep layers toward global context over local atomic property fidelity.
claims.evidence: `a1_step1` MR MLP Drop=13.0 vs Pretrained 13.3; both significantly higher than Random (~1.2). Absolute errors at L12 are ~0.13-0.34, much worse than early layers (Err~0.01).
claims.test: Compare `a1_step1` vs Pretrained on label `mr`. Prediction: Both show MLP Drop > 5 and Best Layer Error < 0.02.
claims.prediction: `mlp_drop` for MR will be ~13 in both models, confirming shared representation dynamics.

trivial_explanations: High performance on binary flags (`aromatic`, `o_neighbor`) may reflect preserved identity features (element type/ring status) that are less susceptible to mixing than continuous property values derived from additive contributions.

The high relative drop metrics for low-error tasks (e.g., 430x for `o_neighbor` linear) are mathematical artifacts of dividing by near-zero baseline errors, not necessarily catastrophic information loss.
